items.headline: FDA Approves First Treatment…
summaries: U.S. Food and Drug Administration reports: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Welgemda (ribitol), the first medicine for treating limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9), a rare inherited muscle disease, for adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg.
U.S. Food and Drug Administration reports: Welgemda is the first therapy approved for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.
U.S. Food and Drug Administration reports: LGMD2I/R9 is caused by mutations in the FKRP gene, which disrupt a key biological process in muscle cells.

items.headline: PCE price increases reported
summaries: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis reports: Personal income increased $201.8 billion (0.7 percent at a monthly rate) in October, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA).

U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis reports: Disposable personal income (DPI)—personal income less personal current taxes—increased $200.5 billion (0.8 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $63.8 billion (0.3 percent).
U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis reports: From the preceding month, the PCE price index for October increased 0.3 percent.

items.headline: SHEIN to Pay $100 Million…
summaries: Federal Trade Commission reports: SHEIN will pay $100 million in consumer redress to settle Federal Trade Commission allegations that the fast-fashion retailer made it unreasonably difficult for consumers to resolve purchase issues, failed to keep its shipping promises, suppressed negative reviews and made deceptive supply chain and cotton-origin claims, all in violation of the law.

Federal Trade Commission reports: In a complaint, the FTC alleges that, through its practices, SHEIN violated Section 5 of the FTC Act, the Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule, and the Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials.

Federal Trade Commission reports: The complaint alleges that SHEIN marketed fast, transparent and reliable shipping but tens of thousands of consumers reported that their orders arrived days, weeks or months late, while some consumers never received their orders at all.
